title: 1956 AHSME Problem 14
statement: The points \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are on a circle \(O.\) The tangent line at \(A\) and the secant \(BC\) intersect at \(P,\) \(B\) lying between \(C\) and \(P.\) If \(BC=20\) and \(PA=10\sqrt3,\) then \(PB\) equals:

solutions.text:
Let \(PB=t.\) Since \(B\) lies between \(P\) and \(C,\) we have \(PC=t+20.\) The tangent-secant theorem gives \[ (10\sqrt3)^2=t(t+20). \] Thus \(t^2+20t-300=0,\) or \((t-10)(t+30)=0.\) A length is positive, so \(t=10.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
